title: Ulyana and the Autopsy
premise: When a confession letter arrives at St. Aldhelm's Cathedral postmarked the day after Mayor Edmund Voss's funeral, archivist Juniper Whitlock discovers the letter names them as its intended recipient — and claims Voss was murdered in the locked crypt beneath the cathedral. Defying the church wardens, the police, and their own twenty-year habit of neutrality, Juniper reopens the case and uncovers that the crypt's seal hides an inheritance scheme stretching back three generations of Vosses. The killer is Corinne Voss, the mayor's sister, who poisoned him to keep the crypt — and the land rights it legally anchors — out of his estranged daughter's hands; Juniper corners her during the equinox reopening of the crypt, where Corinne nearly entombs them both before the confession letter's true author, the dying parish sexton, arrives to testify. In the end Juniper chooses love over duty, leaking the archive they swore to protect to save the daughter, and resigns their post as the crypt is finally opened to daylight.
about_author: Silas Kavanagh is a former parish records clerk from the Yorkshire coast who spent eleven years cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. Ulyana and the Autopsy is his fourth novel, written in a converted tithe barn with a view of a churchyard he refuses to discuss.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Juniper Whitlock's POV. Establishes the cathedral archive, Juniper's meticulous order, and the locked crypt below that even the dean won't enter. A routine morning of filing funeral records for Mayor Edmund Voss ends with an envelope postmarked the day after the burial. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The letter confesses to murder but is unsigned, addressed only as 'To the keeper of what's filed.' It describes Voss's death in the sealed crypt in detail no stranger could know. Juniper photographs it, then burns nothing — yet. Emotional beat: the first crack in twenty years of neutrality.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Know
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper brings the letter to Dean Halloway and warden Ambrose Pell, who dismiss it as a cruel hoax and forbid any inquiry. Pell's hands shake more than grief explains. Emotional beat: institutional stonewalling, and Juniper noticing who protests too much.

chapters.title: The Daughter Returns
chapters.summary: Maren Voss's POV. Edmund's estranged daughter arrives for the reading of the will, sharp-tongued and grieving in ways she won't name. She and Juniper knew each other years ago; old tenderness resurfaces awkwardly. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other across a chasm of time.

chapters.title: A Will Cut Like a Knife
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The will leaves everything to sister Corinne Voss except one clause: Maren inherits 'the undercroft and all rights appurtenant' — the crypt itself. Corinne contests it before the ink dries. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed not as gift but weapon.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Filed Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with flashbacks. Juniper recalls the night twenty years ago when old Aldous Voss died in the same crypt and Juniper, then a young assistant, filed away a document they were told never to read. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body in shallow water.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Cough
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sexton Tobias Marsh, dying of something the doctors can't name, watches Juniper too closely in the churchyard. He leaves a matchbook in the archive marked with the crypt's old key number. Emotional beat: a warning passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Down Where the Air Is Old
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Using the sexton's key, Juniper enters the crypt for the first time and finds Edmund Voss's coffin already disturbed — scratch marks inside the lid, and a second set of footprints in the dust that end mid-stride. Emotional beat: dread made physical.

chapters.title: Corinne's Tea
chapters.summary: Corinne Voss's POV. Charming, brittle Corinne hosts Juniper for tea and probes exactly how much the archivist knows, offering a generous 'archive donation' in exchange for discretion. Emotional beat: power wearing perfume, corruption offered politely.

chapters.title: The Document Juniper Never Read
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finally opens the sealed file from twenty years ago: a deed showing the crypt sits on land whose title transfers only through uninterrupted burial rights — worth millions to whoever controls it. Emotional beat: understanding that the dead are collateral.

chapters.title: Someone Searches My Drawers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The archive has been rifled; the confession letter is gone from its hiding place. Juniper suspects Pell, then catches a glimpse of someone fleeing through the cloister at night. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing they've become the hunted.

chapters.title: Maren's Alibi
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Police detective Okafor interviews Maren, revealing she was in town the day her father died though she claimed otherwise. Juniper lies for her without being asked. Emotional beat: love choosing sides before duty can object.

chapters.title: Tobias Talks
chapters.summary: Sexton Marsh's POV. The dying sexton tells Juniper he saw Corinne enter the crypt the night Edmund died — and that he wrote the confession letter himself, unable to carry it longer. He gives Juniper the original draft hidden in a hymnal. Emotional beat: a man unburdening himself into the grave.

chapters.title: The Draft Disappears
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The hymnal is empty. Someone reached Tobias first; that night he's found unconscious at the bottom of the bell tower stairs. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into fury — the archive's silence has become complicity.

chapters.title: Pell Breaks
chapters.summary: Ambrose Pell's POV. The warden confesses to Juniper that he destroyed the draft on Corinne's instruction — she holds evidence of his own embezzlement from the restoration fund. He agrees to testify if Juniper can guarantee protection. Emotional beat: a small corrupt man choosing, late, to be brave.

chapters.title: Equinox Reopening
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Per tradition, the crypt opens to the public at the autumn equinox — tomorrow. Corinne moves to have the opening cancelled, which would void the deed transfer and erase Maren's claim forever. Emotional beat: the clock becoming audible.

chapters.title: What Juniper Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, reflective midpoint-turn chapter. Juniper confronts their own twenty years of obedient silence and realizes the confession letter was addressed to them because Tobias believed the archivist was the only person with both access and conscience. Emotional beat: duty and love finally forced to declare themselves.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Corinne offers Juniper everything — funding, protection, Maren's safety — if the crypt stays shut. Juniper refuses. That night someone locks Juniper in the archive stacks and sets a small fire. Emotional beat: the cost of refusal, paid in smoke.

chapters.title: Ulyana and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Escaping the fire, Juniper breaks into the crypt before dawn and performs a private examination of Edmund's coffin and remains, finding the arsenic traces and the truth: Edmund was alive when sealed, scratching at the lid. Emotional beat: horror transfigured into resolve — the autopsy that was everyone's duty and no one's job.

chapters.title: The Opening
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. At the equinox ceremony, Juniper halts the proceedings and presents the evidence before the whole town. Corinne, cornered among the tombs, pulls Juniper into the crypt as the doors begin their closing ritual; Pell and Maren force them open. Corinne confesses in front of everyone — not to murder, she insists, but to inheritance. Emotional beat: the crypt opened, literally and morally.

chapters.title: Testimony of a Dying Man
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Tobias, propped up in a hospital bed, gives his testimony; Pell's statement lands; Corinne is charged. The deed passes to Maren, who announces the crypt land will become a public memorial garden. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Daylight in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, final chapter. Juniper resigns the archives, donates the full catalog to the town, and stands with Maren as sunlight enters the opened crypt for the first time in a century. They leave together on the morning train. Emotional beat: love chosen over duty, and the long exhale of a town finally allowed to remember.
